Egypt, Italy and Portugal led export destinations; China and India remained the top suppliers, according to TexPro.
Exports by volume reached 379.485 million kg, while imports stood at 499.016 million kg.

title: Canopy puts forest risk first: What changes for viscose sourcing?
summary:
Canopy’s 2027 Hot Button criteria set an automatic red rating for global MMCF producers with known high-risk forest sourcing.
Low-risk sourcing gets about 31 per cent and Next Gen fibre 27 per cent; policy, traceability and conservation share the rest.
Green Shirt producers are 79 per cent by count but 53 per cent of global MMCF capacity, so buyers must check sourcing and alternatives.

title: Netherlands' unemployment stands at 408,000 in September
summary:
Netherlands' unemployment stood at 408,000 in September, while 3.2 million people were outside the labour force as they were not seeking work or not immediately available.
UWV recorded 197,100 WW unemployment benefit recipients at month-end, up 1.2 per cent month-on-month.
Unemployment rose by an average 5,000 a month over the past three months as more people became unemployed than found work.

title: Rising import costs put ultra-fast fashion’s price edge at risk
summary:
Europe ended the EU €150 exemption for low-value distance-sale consignments on July 1, 2026, adding a temporary €3 duty through July 1, 2028.
A €2 Union handling fee is due from November 1, with multi-item baskets facing charges before VAT.
Low-value imported items reached 5.88 billion in 2025, about 4.2 times 2022, while China accounted for 91 per cent of 2024 volume.

title: Will the US-Bangladesh ART reshape raw material sourcing dynamics?
summary:
The US-Bangladesh Agreement on Reciprocal Trade could give US suppliers a stronger foothold by tying zero-tariff access for some Bangladeshi apparel exports to US-made textile inputs.
Experts say China and India remain entrenched in Bangladesh’s supply chain, with China strong in fabrics and India in yarn.
Cost, proximity and delivery reliability may limit any major sourcing shift.

title: Vietnam's business confidence stays strong in Q3: EuroCham
summary:
EuroCham’s Business Confidence Index for Vietnam reached 78.3 points in Q3 2026, staying historically high despite global economic uncertainty.
The survey found 64 per cent of respondents rated current conditions good or very good, while confidence varied by target market.
Nine in ten would recommend Vietnam for investment; FDI registrations reached $50.36 billion in the first nine months.

title: Yarnproof adds a tracer for origin checks: Will buyers adopt it?
summary:
Unifi and polyester yarn producers across North and Central America have launched YarnProof, a shared tracer system embedded during extrusion to check yarn origin.
The marker can be scanned in yarn, fabric and finished goods, supporting USMCA and CAFTA-DR claims alongside paperwork.
The system is voluntary and does not replace required records or show US Customs approval as stand-alone proof.

title: Bangladesh factory output dips 0.22% in July energy crunch
summary:
Bangladesh’s large-scale industrial production fell 0.22 per cent YoY in July, the opening month of FY2026-27, amid gas and electricity shortages and Middle East tensions. 
Clothing output declined by more than 2 per cent, weighing on the overall index, while textiles grew by over 5 per cent. 
Transport equipment output contracted sharply.

title: The hidden raw material weakness in fashion's $500 bn supply chain
summary:
TrusTrace's October 2026 survey finds trusted supply-chain data falls from 75 per cent at Tier 1 factories to 20 per cent at raw-material and farm level, exposing traceability risk in textile and apparel sourcing.
TexPro shows China, India, Vietnam and Bangladesh moving billions in fabrics, yarn and cotton inputs that brands may need to verify.

title: North India's cotton yarn stable despite rising cotton prices
summary:
North India’s Ludhiana and Delhi cotton yarn prices stayed stable despite cost pressure from higher cotton, as weak downstream demand and payment delays restricted buying.
Panipat recycled yarn was steady, supported by festive home textile demand, but sluggish export orders weighed on sentiment.
Cotton rose ₹150 (~$1.58) per maund as arrivals reached 14,700 bales and ICE futures gained.

title: Luxury’s split market: Ultra-rich spend, aspirational buyers retreat
summary:
Global luxury fashion revenue fell 0.5 per cent in 2025 and is forecast to grow 2.2 per cent in 2026, with growth tapering towards 2031 as aspirational buyers curb spending.
LVMH led luxury goods in 2025 with a 21 per cent share; fashion held 29 per cent, behind watches and jewellery at 34 per cent.
US 2026 revenue is estimated at $96.9 billion, ahead of China at $92.7 billion.

title: Bangladesh's apparel exports to EU may gain in late 2026: Eurostat
summary:
Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the EU could regain momentum late in 2026 and in 2027 as the bloc’s import decline narrows, according to the Eurostat data. 
EU apparel imports fell 3.83 per cent to €60.29 billion (~$67.74 billion) in January-August; Bangladesh’s shipments dropped 11.67 per cent to €11.93 billion (~$13.40 billion). 
August EU import value rose 0.72 per cent year on year.

title: France's Damartex protects profitability amid Q1 revenue decline
summary:
French apparel group Damartex reported an 8 per cent revenue decline to €98.6 million (~$110.68 million) in Q1 FY27 amid hot weather and weak consumer confidence. 
Fashion sales fell as seasonal purchases were delayed, while home and healthcare businesses also declined. 
The group prioritised profitability and operational discipline without disclosing quarterly profit or margin figures.

title: India’s athleisure trend is growing, but sportswear is just 1%
summary:
India’s apparel market is valued at $95.7 billion in 2025, but sportswear holds only about 1 per cent despite athleisure hype and growth expectations.
CMAI-1Lattice data shows men lead sportswear at $630 million, ahead of kids at $250 million and women at $150 million.
Among men, 17 per cent of track pant or suit buyers bought online, while major offline chains already stock the category.

title: Hong Kong’s T-shirt imports defy wider apparel decline
summary:

Jerseys slipped to second, while trousers and shorts fell 8.23 per cent and shirts dropped 11.29 per cent, according to TexPro.
Home textile imports rose 7.91 per cent to $179.265 million, led by bed textiles.

title: Vietnam’s export growth masks margin crunch?
summary:
Vietnam’s textile and garment exports hit nearly $31.7 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up 2.9 per cent year on year, but profitability remains squeezed.
Smaller batches, tighter deadlines and buyer delays are weakening scale economies and order visibility.
Logistics costs of 9–10 per cent of export-import value, congestion and surcharges make delivery efficiency crucial.

title: UK’s garment exports dip 10% in August 2026
summary:
United Kingdom clothing exports fell 10.1 per cent year on year to £214 million (~$282 million) in August 2026, ONS data showed, easing from £235 million in July.
Textile fabric exports dropped 10.41 per cent to £172 million, while fibre exports rose year on year to £39 million but fell from July.
In Q2 2026, clothing exports slipped 1.93 per cent to £711 million, with 2025 exports down 9.17 per cent.

title: UK’s clothing imports down 10% in Aug 2026
summary:
UK clothing imports fell 10.37 per cent YoY to £1.494 billion (~$1.966 billion) in August 2026 but rose 4.76 per cent from July.
Fabric imports dropped 4.33 per cent YoY and 18.79 per cent monthly to £419 million; fibre imports stood at £22 million.
Q2 2026 clothing imports fell 3.67 per cent, while full-year 2025 imports rose 6.05 per cent.

title: EU traceability push puts Bangladesh’s SMEs to the test
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment SMEs could face a disproportionate burden from EU traceability and DPP rules as they invest in data collection, verification, system integration and training.
Stakeholders seek clearer rules, coordinated data systems, targeted financing and enough preparation time to prevent smaller suppliers bearing excessive compliance costs.

title: US annual inflation rises to 3.7% in Sept; apparel prices up 3.4%
summary:
US annual consumer inflation accelerated to 3.7 per cent in September 2026 from 3.4 per cent in August, according to BLS data. 
Monthly inflation rose 0.6 per cent, driven by a 9.1 per cent surge in gasoline prices. 
Apparel prices increased 0.3 per cent monthly and 3.4 per cent annually, while core inflation reached 2.6 per cent year on year.
